key_results: SLK is cancer-specific c-Myc interactor; SLK phosphorylates c-Myc at S329, antagonizing GSK3β-mediated phosphodegron phosphorylation; long SLK isoform promotes nuclear localization and c-Myc target expression across tumor types
comments: Context-dependent photoproximity labeling is innovative and enables cancer-specific targeting, though the clinical translation of SLK inhibition remains unvalidated.

Cancer cell lines and patient data

hypotheses.hypothesis: SLK stabilizes c-Myc by antagonizing GSK3β-dependent phosphodegron phosphorylation
hypotheses.result: SLK phosphorylates c-Myc at S329; this antagonizes GSK3β-mediated degradation; SLK is cancer-specific and essential for tumorigenesis

hypotheses.hypothesis: Splicing produces long SLK isoform associated with cancer phenotype and c-Myc activity
hypotheses.result: Long SLK isoform promotes nuclear localization and drives c-Myc target expression across tumor types

title: 4-Hydroxytamoxifen suppresses the malignant progression of lung adenocarcinoma by inhibiting MAPK signaling pathway
task: Identify and validate 4-hydroxytamoxifen as an anti-tumor agent inhibiting MAPK-mediated lipid metabolism in lung adenocarcinoma
key_results: 4-OHT inhibited MEK/ERK phosphorylation, downregulated fatty acid metabolism genes, reduced intracellular lipids, and suppressed subcutaneous tumor growth in vivo; MAPK activation reversed growth inhibition
comments: Drug repurposing strategy is promising, but the contribution of lipid metabolism inhibition versus direct MAPK suppression to apoptosis induction needs clarification.

hypotheses.hypothesis: 4-OHT suppresses LUAD progression by inhibiting MAPK-mediated lipid metabolism
hypotheses.result: 4-OHT downregulated fatty acid metabolism genes and lipid metabolites; MAPK activation reversed 4-OHT-induced lipid deficiency and growth inhibition

title: Combination treatment with quantum molecular resonance and secretome attenuates the chimeric transcript response to oxidative stress in retinal pigment epithelial cells
task: Characterize chimeric transcript burden as a measurable phenotype of oxidative stress in retinal pigment epithelial cells and test therapeutic reversal
key_results: Oxidative stress increased chimeric transcript burden by 33% (IRR 1.33, p=0.002); combined QMR+secretome treatment reversed stress-induced chimeras (IRR 0.40, p=0.007); stress preferentially induced frame-preserving, translatable chimeras (p=0.028)
comments: Rigorous statistical framework and orthogonal validation of CTDNEP1-ENSG00000262526 junction strengthen findings, but the biological consequences of translatable chimeric proteins remain speculative.

model_io.model: ARPE-19 retinal pigment epithelial cells (n=72 samples, factorial design)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Oxidative stress increases chimeric transcript burden via non-random, frame-preferential mechanisms
hypotheses.result: Stress increased chimeric burden by 33%; induced chimeras preferentially preserve reading frame (2.59-fold enrichment)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Combined QMR+secretome treatment reverses stress-induced but not constitutive chimeric junctions
hypotheses.result: Combined therapy reversed stress-induced chimeras (IRR 0.40) but not constitutive controls (p=0.49)

title: Cysteine preconditioning improves post-freeze-thaw proliferative capacity of human synovial mesenchymal stem cells
task: Determine whether L-cysteine preconditioning improves post-freeze-thaw proliferative recovery in synovial mesenchymal stem cells
key_results: Cysteine preconditioning increased post-freeze-thaw cell numbers and colony formation in 3/6 donors (mixed-effects p<0.05); GSH responsiveness correlated with recovery (r=0.95 for cell number, r=0.91 for colonies)
comments: Donor-dependent heterogeneity in response limits broad applicability; mechanistic link between GSH and proliferation capacity remains incompletely characterized.

model_io.model: Human synovial MSCs from osteoarthritis patients (n=6)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cysteine preconditioning improves post-thaw proliferation via increased intracellular GSH
hypotheses.result: Cysteine increased GSH in all donors; GSH responsiveness strongly correlated with post-thaw cell number and colony formation recovery

task: Characterize exciton engineering in TMD/2D magnet heterostructures
key_results: Identified proximity-induced interlayer magnetic excitons with energy ~1.98–1.99 eV across stacking variants; revealed stacking-dependent oscillator strengths and interlayer decompositions
comments: Parameter-free GW calculations provide high-fidelity reference, though practical device engineering from these insights remains unexplored.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Proximity effects modify Wannier-Mott excitons in WSe2 sensitively while creating robust interlayer magnetic excitons
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; interlayer exciton energy nearly constant across stacking but oscillator strength varies with structure

title: Spintronics in cluster-assembled one-dimensional materials with a screw dislocation
task: Design spintronic 1D nanowires from cluster assembly with engineered spin textures
key_results: Designed 8 cluster-assembled nanowires with pronounced Rashba SOC (Re-based) and substantial Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interactions (Mn-based); demonstrated energetic, thermal and dynamic stability
comments: Screw dislocation-induced inversion symmetry breaking is elegant; experimental synthesis of such cluster chains remains challenging.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Helical screw dislocations intrinsically break inversion symmetry and enable SOC-induced spin textures
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by DFT; both Re and Mn systems show robust spin-orbit effects without external fields

title: Spontaneous emergence of skyrmions beyond room temperature in boron-doped CrTe
task: Observe zero-field skyrmion stabilization in boron-doped CrTe beyond room temperature
key_results: Spontaneous skyrmions observed >300 K without external field; robust over large temperature and thickness ranges; field-cooling controls skyrmion density
comments: Direct observation via Lorentz TEM is definitive; mechanism for zero-field stabilization in centrosymmetric lattice warrants further investigation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Boron doping stabilizes skyrmions without external field and above room temperature
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; metastable zero-field skyrmions observed with controllable density via field-cooling

title: Positron annihilation spectroscopy
task: Review positron annihilation spectroscopy techniques and defect characterization
key_results: Positron spectroscopy enables atomic-scale vacancy structure identification, concentration measurement, and property determination across diverse materials; recent advances span defects, porosity, surfaces, and interfaces
comments: Comprehensive review of experimental methods and applications; positron source brightness remains limiting factor for sub-nanosecond temporal resolution.

model_io.model: Positron annihilation spectroscopy (PAS) with γ-photon detection

hypotheses.hypothesis: Selective positron sensitivity to vacancies enables detailed defect characterization unavailable to other probes
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; multiple techniques (lifetime, angular correlation, Doppler broadening) provide complementary defect signatures
